included: read-back of the frozen admission, semantic-gate, effective-eight supplement, measurement state, 56 cell records, 56 raw reports, and 112 captured streams
independent verification of file seals, cell identities, commands, seed order, worker and observation envelopes, warmup evidence, and content-digest stability
independent recomputation of all 16 primary timing, throughput, paired-speedup, paired-efficiency, stage, cold-wall, and RSS distributions
independent verification of all eight startup-probe records
independent monitoring-log cadence and observed-process review
excluded: no model, compiler, runtime, benchmark, build, or test was rerun
no claim of exclusive CPU isolation or zero background load
no cross-backend comparison of Rust serde byte hashes with PyO3 JSON byte hashes
no native Windows acceptance and no remote CI acceptance
the public archive excludes host-sensitive local monitoring and machine snapshots, so a public-archive consumer cannot independently repeat the monitoring review from the archive alone
no claim beyond this exact machine, run, frozen Plan, seed list, and timing protocol

measurement_inventory.composition: 56 each of record.json, raw-report.json, stdout.txt, and stderr.txt
measurement_inventory.digest_algorithm: SHA-256 over lexicographically sorted UTF-8 lines: relative_path<TAB>decimal_bytes<TAB>file_sha256<LF>

cell_evidence.commands: all 56 equal their recorded execution command and carry the scheduled backend, observation level, worker count, and exact seed prefix under taskset CPUs 0-7
cell_evidence.seals: all 168 cell-referenced raw-report, stdout, and stderr files match the recorded size and SHA-256; the 56 record files were structurally checked and included with those files in the independent 224-file inventory digest
cell_evidence.warmups: all cells record one completed warmup; PyO3 warmup and measured proofs are identical; Rust explicitly retains no warmup digest and does not claim one
cell_evidence.cross_envelope_content: stable within each backend, observation level, and sample-count group

pyo3_result_hashes.algorithm: SHA-256 of each result encoded as UTF-8 JSON with ensure_ascii=false, sorted keys, compact separators, and non-finite numbers rejected
pyo3_result_hashes.comparison: every measured and warmup per-sample digest matches the admitted event-time-v2 Full or Summary result for its seed 0, 1, or 7
pyo3_result_hashes.scope_note: these are PyO3-boundary canonical JSON hashes, not Rust serde-byte hashes

effective_eight_supplement.complete_decoded_tree_equality: Rust equals PyO3 for each Full and Summary batch; every sample equals the corresponding already-admitted seed result
effective_eight_supplement.serialization_note: decoded semantic trees were compared; the distinct Rust and PyO3 file hashes are retained and were not misrepresented as cross-backend byte equality

summary_recomputation.comparison: independent recomputation matched summary.json recursively, including warm timing, samples/second, same-repeat worker-1 speedup, efficiency, stage timing, cold process wall time, and RSS distributions
summary_recomputation.distribution: median, minimum, maximum, and median absolute deviation
summary_recomputation.startup_probes: all eight summary entries are exact copies of the independently verified completed cell records

monitoring_review.evidence_availability: local audit only: window-known-tools.log and window-top.log were read from the unchanged local run but are intentionally excluded from the public archive because host process command lines can contain unrelated personal paths; their hashes remain recorded here
monitoring_review.verdict: no competing build, test, or benchmark was observed by the retained known-tool scans; monitoring does not establish exclusive or noise-free execution

known_tool_scans.cadence_disclosure: the local log retains two manual snapshots at 06:06:23Z and 06:07:13Z; the automated approximately 30-second sequence began at 06:08:12Z; observed later gaps were 30 or 31 seconds

top_snapshots.cadence: 175 adjacent gaps were 5 seconds and seven were 6 seconds

monitoring_review.observed_background_activity: retained top snapshots include constant remote-control, network, editor, and Codex processes; one Codex snapshot reached 22.2% CPU and the VS Code extension host reached 29.0% CPU with four snapshots at or above 10%. CPU affinity is not present in top output, so these observations cannot be converted into a claim about contention on CPUs 0-7.
monitoring_review.interpretation: timing results are valid observations under the recorded shared-host conditions, not proof of exclusive-host peak performance

final_statement: The frozen run is internally consistent and its published summary is arithmetically reproducible from the sealed records. Acceptance is limited to data integrity and protocol-consistent reporting for this exact run.
